related_questions.question: How does a US citizen get a visa for India?

text_blocks.snippet: A U.S. citizen can get a visa for India by applying online for an e-Visa or through the Indian Embassy or a designated Indian Visa Application Center. The e-Visa is a faster option for eligible categories like tourism, business, or medical visits, while a regular visa application involves a more traditional process.
snippet_highlighted_words: by applying online for an e-Visa or through the Indian Embassy or a designated Indian Visa Application Center

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of the two methods:

list.title: Eligibility:
list.snippet: U.S. citizens can apply for an e-Visa for various purposes including tourism, business, medical visits (including medical attendant), and conferences.

list.title: Application:
list.snippet: Apply online through the official Indian e-Visa portal.
Complete the online application form.
Upload necessary documents like passport copy and photograph.
Pay the e-Visa fee online.
Receive the Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) via email.
Print the ETA and present it at the designated immigration check post in India, where it will be stamped in your passport.
Ensure your passport has at least six months of validity from your arrival date in India and has blank pages.
You must travel on the same passport that the e-Visa was issued for.
The e-Visa is valid for a limited number of entry points, including designated airports and seaports.
Apply online through the Indian Visa Online portal and choose the "Regular Visa Application" option.
Complete the application form online.

Submit the application along with required documents (e.g., passport, photos, proof of financial means, travel itinerary, etc.) to an Indian Visa Application Center or the Indian Mission (Embassy or Consulate).
The Indian Mission or Visa Application Center will review your application and supporting documents.
An interview may be scheduled.
If approved, your passport with the visa will be returned to you.

list.title: Registration:
list.snippet: Foreigners staying in India for more than 180 days on long-term visas (student, medical, or employment) need to register with the relevant Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO) or Foreigners Registration Officer (FRO) within 14 days of arrival.

list.title: Exemptions:
list.snippet: Individuals with a valid OCI card or those who are exempt under bilateral agreements may not need a visa.

list.title: Official Websites:
list.snippet: Always use the official Indian government websites for visa applications to avoid scams.

related_questions.question: How much does an India visa cost?

text_blocks.snippet: The cost of an Indian visa for US citizens varies depending on the type of visa and its validity. For e-Tourist visas, a 30-day visa costs $25, a one-year visa costs $40, and a five-year visa costs $80, according to the Consulate General of India, San Francisco. Traditional tourist visas for US citizens can range from $160 to $250, depending on whether it's a single or multiple entry visa. Other visa types like business, student, and medical visas have different fees, with business visas costing $250 and student visas costing $120, according to Passports and Visas.

related_questions.question: How long does it take to get an India visa?

text_blocks.snippet: The time it takes to get an Indian visa varies, but e-visas for tourism, business, or medical purposes typically take 3-5 working days for standard processing and 1-3 working days for urgent processing. For other visa types like student, conference, or journalist visas, processing times can range from a few days to several weeks.
snippet_highlighted_words: 3-5 working days for standard processing and 1-3 working days for urgent processing

list.snippet: Visa Type: Tourist, business, and medical e-visas are generally processed faster than student, conference, or work visas.
Processing Method: Standard processing times are longer than urgent or express processing options.
Nationality: Some nationalities may require additional verification or processing time.
Application Completeness: Incomplete applications can lead to delays.

list.snippet: e-Tourist Visa: 3-5 working days for standard processing, 1-3 for urgent.

Work Visa: Can take up to 10 days for a 180-day validity visa.

text_blocks.snippet: To obtain an Indian visa, you'll generally need to apply online, submit required documents, and potentially schedule an appointment at an Indian Visa Application Center. The specific process and requirements vary depending on your nationality and the type of visa you need.
snippet_highlighted_words: apply online, submit required documents, and potentially schedule an appointment at an Indian Visa Application Center

list.snippet: Tourist Visa: For recreational travel, sightseeing, or visiting friends/relatives.
Business Visa: For business-related activities.
Medical Visa: For medical treatment.
Other visa types: There are also options for student visas, employment visas, and more.
Most visa applications are now done online through the Indian government website.
You'll need to create an account, fill out the application form, and upload required documents.
Ensure all information is accurate and matches your passport.
Gather all necessary documents, such as your passport, photos, and any supporting documents specific to your visa type.
For example, a business visa may require an invitation letter or proof of business registration.
For a medical visa, you'll need a letter from a hospital or doctor in India.
Some visa applications may require you to schedule an appointment at an Indian Visa Application Center (IVAC).
Check the website of your local Indian embassy or consulate for details on where to submit your application and if an appointment is necessary.
Visa fees vary depending on your nationality and the type of visa.
You can find the fee structure on the Indian embassy or consulate website or the VFS Global website.
Most visa application websites allow you to track the progress of your application.
You can also contact the Indian embassy or consulate for updates.
Once your visa is approved, you will receive it either by mail or you will need to pick it up from the Indian Visa Application Center.
For e-visas, you will receive an electronic travel authorization.
